questions.question: If you must stop quickly while in a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Straighten the handlebars and then stop.
Apply both brakes hard while leaning.
Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten the handlebars and then stop.
questions.explanation: If you must stop quickly in a curve, straighten and square the handlebars first, then stop. If you cannot straighten the motorcycle, apply the brakes smoothly, reduce your lean angle, then brake harder as you slow down.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve around the dog.
Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest.
Ride next to the dog.
Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up and leave it behind.
questions.explanation: If a dog is chasing you, downshift and approach it slowly. Then accelerate and ride away from it.

questions.question: When riding in rain or fog, what headlight should you use?

options.text: Your high beam.
Your low beam.
No headlight.
Switch between low and high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your low beam.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in rain, snow, or fog. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder for you to see.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids from braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the front brake engaged.
Release the front brake right away, then reapply it smoothly.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then reapply it smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks up from braking, release the front brake immediately and then reapply it smoothly.

questions.question: How can you keep other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Swerve side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to share it with you.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders together.
Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
Use only your mirrors.
Move only your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Should motorcycle riders wear hearing protection?

options.text: Yes, always to prevent hearing damage.
Only on long rides.
No, because it blocks horns and sirens.
No, if you wear a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, always to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise cause permanent hearing damage over time, even with a full-face helmet. Earplugs provide protection while still allowing you to hear horns and sirens.

questions.question: How does a motorcycle's stopping distance compare to a car's?

options.text: Cars take much longer to stop.
Cars take a little longer to stop.
Motorcycles take longer to stop.
They take about the same time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take about the same time to stop.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, motorcycles and cars have nearly the same stopping distance. However, slippery pavement makes it much harder for motorcycles to stop quickly.

questions.question: In a slow, tight turn, what should the rider do with their body?

options.text: Keep their body upright while the motorcycle leans.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean in the opposite direction of the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright while leaning their body.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep their body upright while the motorcycle leans.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, lean at the same angle as your motorcycle. In slow, tight turns, keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which instruction is wrong?

options.text: The passenger should get on after the engine starts.
The passenger should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.
The passenger should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.
The passenger can talk whenever they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passenger can talk whenever they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should avoid talking or moving while you ride to keep you focused. Passengers should get on only after the engine starts, sit as far forward as possible without crowding you, and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: How should a rider sit to best control a motorcycle?

options.text: With arms fully extended.
Using arms to hold the body up.
With knees away from the gas tank.
With feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: With feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Use your arms to control the motorcycle, not to hold yourself up. Keep your arms slightly bent. Press your knees against the gas tank and keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists ride when entering a highway or curve?

options.text: Single-file.
In a staggered formation.
In pairs.
In the far right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation normally, but switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Ride in single-file formation.
The group will exit at the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in single-file formation.
questions.explanation: When the lead rider raises their left arm and points their index finger up, the group should move into single-file formation.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when being passed from behind?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. This discourages the other driver from re-entering your lane too soon.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Planning to turn left.
About to stop.
Planning to turn right.
About to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Planning to turn right.
questions.explanation: A bent left arm pointing upward means the rider plans to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: What setting should your headlight use during the day?

options.text: Should not be used.
High beam setting.
Low beam setting.
Alternating between high and low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: High beam setting.
questions.explanation: Use your high beam headlight during the day to help other drivers see you. Use high beam any time you are not directly behind or approaching other vehicles.

questions.question: Where should cargo be placed on a motorcycle?

options.text: As low as possible.
As high as possible.
Behind the rear axle.
On one side of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep cargo low and secure it or place it in saddlebags. High loads raise the center of gravity and affect balance. Distribute cargo equally on both sides.

questions.question: What is the minimum safe following distance when riding at night?

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.
Five seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: Night riding makes it harder to see and judge distances. Keep at least three seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. This gives you more time to see and react to stops.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Rest stop.
High beams on.
Turn right.
Hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hazard.
questions.explanation: When the lead rider extends their right leg, it means there is a hazard on the right side of the road.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning.
Service.
Regulatory.
Speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black lettering or symbols are warning signs. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Help you see better.
Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Give you a way to escape danger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see better and be seen. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your lane position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Speed up.
Leave the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane is especially slippery when wet. When rain starts, avoid the center by riding in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is usually the best choice.

questions.question: Maximum straight-line braking is done by:

options.text: Using the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Using the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Using both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Using both brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: Maximum straight-line braking means using both the front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.

questions.question: Do not change gears on railroad tracks because:

options.text: Your motorcycle may stall.
You might go too fast.
Other drivers may not expect you to change gears.
The uneven surface makes it harder to shift gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may stall.
questions.explanation: Do not shift gears when crossing railroad tracks. Your motorcycle might stall while you are on the tracks.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, EXCEPT:

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.
Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid road hazards.
Block your escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block your escape route.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see better and be seen. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your lane position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.
